topic_tag: wolves and a wintering elk herd
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Over the decade that followed, the pack ______ the herd.

worlds.passage: When wolves returned to a mountain valley in 1995, a pack of nine settled along the creek where a herd of four hundred elk spends each winter. Over the decade that followed, the pack ______ the herd. The elk it killed were mostly old cows and lame calves, and their carcasses lay scattered across the open benches in every direction, often two miles from the willow thickets where the herd had been feeding that morning. The herd spent its evenings in those thickets, and its calves were born there each spring.
worlds.explanation: "Chased" fits: the wolves took the slowest elk, old cows and lame calves, and the carcasses lay up to two miles from where the herd had been feeding, so the wolves ran elk down until the weakest fell behind. "Ambushed" fails because an attack from hiding takes whatever elk passes the hiding place, at close range; these kills fell on open benches far from the herd's feeding ground and picked out the weakest, which is what a pursuit does. "Corralled" fails because the carcasses lay in every direction, so the wolves were not driving the herd into any one place. "Cowed" fails because the herd kept spending its evenings in the thickets and calving there, so the wolves did not frighten it out of its habits.

ambushed.quote: scattered across the open benches in every direction
ambushed.why: kills on open ground far from where the herd fed, chosen by weakness
ambushed.surface_fit: wolves are often described lying in wait, and a pack settled along the creek where the elk winter suggests a hidden attack
ambushed.inference: a predator striking from cover kills whatever passes its hiding place, close by; carcasses spread over open benches two miles from the morning's feeding ground, almost all old or lame, are the end of runs that the slowest lost

corralled.why: no single place where the herd was driven
corralled.surface_fit: a pack of nine working a herd together suggests driving the elk into a trap, a familiar picture of pack hunting
corralled.inference: if the kills lay in every direction across the benches, each hunt ended wherever a straggler fell, so the wolves were not pushing the herd toward any confining place

cowed.quote: its calves were born there each spring
cowed.why: the herd kept using the thickets
cowed.surface_fit: the return of wolves is widely reported to have frightened elk out of creekside willows
cowed.inference: a herd that spends its evenings in the thickets and drops its calves there each spring, with the wolves living along the same creek, has not been frightened out of its habits

worlds.passage: When wolves returned to a mountain valley in 1995, a pack of nine settled along the creek where a herd of four hundred elk spends each winter. Over the decade that followed, the pack ______ the herd. Collars showed the wolves spending their days in the creek's willow thickets where the herd's trails cross it. Nearly every carcass lay on one of those trails within a few yards of the water, and the dead included prime bulls as often as old cows. Each evening the herd filed down from the open benches along the same trails to drink, and the willows beside them were cropped to knee height.
worlds.explanation: "Ambushed" fits: the wolves lay all day in thickets at the trail crossings, the herd came down those trails every evening, and the kills fell right there, so the wolves waited hidden for the elk to come to them. "Chased" fails because the kills lay within yards of the thickets and took prime bulls as often as old cows; a pursuit ends far off and takes the slowest. "Corralled" fails because the herd walked down to the crossings on its own each evening, so nothing drove it there. "Cowed" fails because the herd kept filing down the very trails where it lost animals and cropping the willows beside them.

chased.quote: prime bulls as often as old cows
chased.why: kills at the thicket edge took strong and weak alike
chased.surface_fit: wolves are best known as pursuit hunters, so chased is the obvious verb for a pack and a herd
chased.inference: a chase is lost by the slowest animal and ends wherever it falls behind; kills within yards of the thickets that take prime bulls as often as old cows came from close-range strikes, not runs

corralled.quote: Each evening the herd filed down from the open benches
corralled.why: the elk came to the spot by themselves
corralled.surface_fit: a pack picking the spot where its prey gathers sounds like hemming the herd into a trap
corralled.inference: the herd walked down its own trails to drink every evening while the wolves lay in the thickets, so the pack moved nothing; the elk came to the place themselves

cowed.quote: the willows beside them were cropped to knee height
cowed.why: the elk kept feeding at the dangerous crossings
cowed.surface_fit: wolves returning to a valley are widely said to have frightened elk away from creeks
cowed.inference: elk that file down the trails where they are killed and crop the willows beside them to knee height are still feeding at the crossings, so fear has not changed where they go

worlds.passage: When wolves returned to a mountain valley in 1995, a pack of nine settled along the creek where a herd of four hundred elk spends each winter. Over the decade that followed, the pack ______ the herd. In deep snow the wolves spread out in a wide arc on the open benches and walked slowly toward the elk, which moved off ahead of them downhill into a side canyon where drifts lay chest-deep; there, floundering, several fell in an afternoon to wolves trotting on the crust. By spring the elk were back grazing the benches and the willows along the creek.
worlds.explanation: "Corralled" fits: walking in a wide arc, the wolves pushed the elk ahead of them into a canyon of chest-deep drifts, a confined place where they could not escape. "Chased" fails because the wolves walked slowly and the elk moved off ahead of them, so the kills came from where the elk were pushed, not from outrunning them. "Ambushed" fails because the wolves came at the herd in the open, spread across the benches in plain sight, instead of waiting hidden. "Cowed" fails because by spring the elk were back on the benches and in the creek willows, so the pack did not frighten them out of their range.

chased.why: the wolves walked; the elk moved ahead and were trapped by the drifts, not run down
chased.surface_fit: the wolves trot on the crust and the elk move away from them, which reads at first like a pursuit
chased.inference: wolves walking slowly in an arc push the elk ahead rather than overtaking them, and the elk died only once the canyon drifts held them, so position, not pursuit, decided the hunt

ambushed.quote: spread out in a wide arc on the open benches
ambushed.why: the wolves approached in open view rather than lying hidden
ambushed.surface_fit: elk dying in a side canyon sounds like a trap sprung on them, which is what an ambush is
ambushed.inference: a line of wolves walking across open benches is visible to the elk the whole time, and the elk moved away from it, so the attack did not come from concealment

cowed.quote: back grazing the benches and the willows
cowed.why: the elk resumed their old range by spring
cowed.surface_fit: the frightening effect of wolves on elk is famous, so cowed fits both the topic and the sentence
cowed.inference: if the elk return to the same benches and creek willows once the snow goes, the pack has not changed where they live or feed, so they were not intimidated

worlds.passage: When wolves returned to a mountain valley in 1995, a pack of nine settled along the creek where a herd of four hundred elk spends each winter. Over the decade that followed, the pack ______ the herd. It killed fewer than thirty elk a year, most of them on the open benches above the creek. Elk that once grazed for hours in the willow thickets began to pass through them without stopping, heads up, even when collars placed the pack thirty miles off, and fed in scattered bands on the benches, lifting their heads every few bites. By 2005 willows long held to knee height stood taller than a rider.
worlds.explanation: "Cowed" fits: the pack killed few elk, yet the herd stopped lingering in the thickets, stayed watchful while feeding, and kept doing so even when the wolves were thirty miles off, so the wolves changed the herd's behavior through fear. "Chased" fails because the elk avoided the thickets in weeks when no wolf was near them, so no pursuit was pushing them out. "Ambushed" fails because most kills were on the open benches, away from the thickets that could have hidden a wolf. "Corralled" fails because the elk fed in scattered bands across the benches, so they were spread out rather than confined.

chased.quote: even when collars placed the pack thirty miles off
chased.why: the elk kept avoiding the thickets with no wolves anywhere near
chased.surface_fit: the elk moved out of the willow thickets onto the benches, which looks like being driven out by wolves, and chasing is what wolves are known for
chased.inference: elk that trot through the thickets while the pack is thirty miles away are not being pursued at that moment, so their move to the benches comes from fear, not from being run off

ambushed.quote: most of them on the open benches
ambushed.why: kills happened on open ground, not at the thickets
ambushed.surface_fit: elk avoiding dense willows is what one would expect if wolves were lying in wait there, so ambushed is a natural guess
ambushed.inference: if most kills fell on the open benches, away from the thickets where a wolf could hide, the pack was not killing from cover

corralled.why: the herd spread out across the benches
corralled.surface_fit: a pack and a herd suggest wolves herding elk together into one place, so corralled fits the sentence
corralled.inference: a herd split into scattered bands across open benches has been dispersed, not gathered into a confined place, so the wolves did not pen it
